plan.title: Vendor email when bid is rejected

steps.note: Create a test event for the rejection scenario.
Every publishable event requires a title.
Use an RFQ stage so vendor bids can be submitted and rejected.
Apply the RFQ pricing template before adding line items.
Provide a product for the vendor bids.
Commit a bidding schedule before publishing.
Invite two QA vendors so one rejection can be compared with an unaffected vendor.
Publish the test event before collecting bids.
Confirm the event reached a real published project page.
Submit a bid from the first QA vendor.
Confirm the first vendor's bid was accepted.
Submit a bid from a second QA vendor so another vendor remains unaffected by the rejection.
Confirm the second vendor's bid was accepted.
Close bidding so the buyer can process the submitted bids.

args.goal: on the buyer's Responses screen, reject exactly one QA vendor bid with a buyer reason while leaving the other vendor's bid active; stop when the rejection is visibly saved

steps.note: The catalog has no dedicated bid-rejection action, so use the buyer screen to perform and verify the rejection.

args.need: open the QA mailboxes, verify the rejected vendor received exactly one rejection email containing the buyer's reason, and verify no other vendor or real supplier received it

steps.note: Mailbox access and email-recipient verification are not available in the catalog.
Confirm the buyer session has no application error after the rejection workflow.
